prompt: What makes a group of machines one trust zone?
hint: One rule should speak for all of them.

choices.text: They share one switch
choices.why: A cable is not a trust decision.

choices.text: They face the same risks and deserve the same trust
choices.why: Right, so one rule speaks for all.

choices.text: They run the same operating system
choices.why: That says nothing about who uses them or what they hold.

choices.text: They were bought at the same time
choices.why: Irrelevant to trust.

prompt: Match what probe printed to what happened.
hint: The table in the section.

pairs.right: a machine answered that nothing listens there
nothing came back within a second

right_distractors: the host name did not resolve

prompt: Why is the staff LAN trusted less than the servers segment?
hint: Who uses the machines?

choices.text: Its machines are cheaper, so losing one costs less
choices.why: Price is not the reason.

choices.text: It has more machines
choices.why: Size is not the reason.

choices.text: People on it open attachments and browse the web
choices.why: Right. That is how problems arrive.

choices.text: It faces the internet directly, the way the DMZ does
choices.why: It is not; the DMZ is.

prompt: Which statements describe a DMZ? Choose all that apply.
hint: The three directions.

choices.text: The internet may reach it on the services it offers
choices.why: That is what it is for.

choices.text: It reaches the inside only where a service needs it
choices.why: One address and one port at a time.

choices.text: The inside is reachable from the internet through the DMZ's routing
choices.why: The inside is reached only through something in the DMZ, never routed to.

choices.text: It is trusted as much as the servers segment
choices.why: It is trusted by neither side.

prompt: What does a DMZ between two firewalls buy over one firewall with three legs?
hint: A flaw in one box.

choices.text: Lower cost and less upkeep
choices.why: It costs more: two boxes, two rule sets.

choices.text: A second layer that still stands if one fails
choices.why: Right, at the price of a second policy.

choices.text: It removes the need for a rule set on the inner side
choices.why: The inner firewall needs rules of its own.

choices.text: It lets the DMZ reach the internet freely
choices.why: Egress is a policy choice, not a shape.

prompt: DMZ is short for demilitarised ___.
hint: The last word of the name.

prompt: In the zone matrix, the servers row is empty. What does that mean?
hint: A row is what a zone may start.

choices.text: Nothing may reach the servers
choices.why: That would be the column, and it has entries.

choices.text: The servers start no conversation with other zones
choices.why: Right. They answer and never call out.

choices.text: The servers row has not been decided by anybody yet
choices.why: Empty cells are decided: they mean denied.

choices.text: Replies from the servers are dropped before they leave
choices.why: Replies are established traffic, not new conversations.

prompt: The DMZ-to-servers rule names ip saddr 192.0.2.80 as well as the destination. What does naming the source add?
hint: dns is in the DMZ too.

choices.text: Nothing, since the interface already says the packet came from the DMZ
choices.why: The interface admits every machine in the DMZ.

choices.text: It makes the rule faster to match
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

choices.text: It lets replies from app return to the proxy
choices.why: established,related already does that.

choices.text: Only the proxy, of all the DMZ machines, gets through to app
choices.why: Right. A compromised dns still gets nowhere.

prompt: How many commented accept rules does the forward chain of baseline.nft have?
hint: Count the lines with a comment; the established,related rule has none.

prompt: Why does the staff's DNS rule allow TCP as well as UDP?
hint: Some answers do not fit.

choices.text: DNS falls back to TCP for large answers
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: dnsmasq accepts nothing but TCP
choices.why: dig used UDP and was answered.

choices.text: TCP is needed for the reply to come back
choices.why: UDP replies return as established.

choices.text: It is a mistake the lesson corrects later
choices.why: It is deliberate.

prompt: From remote, probe said dns:53 blocked, yet dig from remote got an answer. Why both?
hint: Which transport does each use?

choices.text: The DNS server was restarted between the two commands
choices.why: Nothing was restarted.

choices.text: probe waits only one second
choices.why: A timeout does not explain an allowed UDP answer.

choices.text: probe tries TCP, and the internet's cell allows UDP
choices.why: Right. The matrix working as written.

choices.text: dig went through the proxy on www
choices.why: dig asked 192.0.2.53 directly.

prompt: From admin, probe said www:22 refused. What does that tell you about the firewall?
hint: Who sent the refusal?

choices.text: The firewall refused it
choices.why: A drop sends nothing; the policy is drop.

choices.text: It let the connection through; www runs no SSH
choices.why: Right. refused came from www itself.

choices.text: The rule for management is missing
choices.why: Then it would say blocked.

choices.text: www is down
choices.why: It served HTTPS in the same lesson.

prompt: When should the matrix test be run again? Choose all that apply.
hint: A claim is checked by trying it.

choices.text: After any change to the rule set
choices.why: A hurried rule opens cells by accident.

choices.text: After a new server is added to a zone
choices.why: It inherits the zone's cells.

choices.text: After a firewall upgrade
choices.why: What the rules do is what gets tested.

choices.text: Only when an incident is reported
choices.why: By then the cell has been open for a while.

prompt: After www is compromised, what can the attacker reach from it?
hint: probe from www.

choices.text: The database, through the proxy rule
choices.why: db:5432 was blocked from www.

choices.text: app on 8080, and nothing else
choices.why: Right. One door.

choices.text: The internet, to call home for instructions
choices.why: remote:80 and remote:443 were blocked.

choices.text: The management segment and its SSH port
choices.why: admin:22 was blocked.

prompt: Why does it matter that the DMZ has no row towards the internet?
hint: What does software that takes over a server do next?

choices.text: It saves bandwidth on the internet link
choices.why: A side effect at most.

choices.text: Replies to the internet's visitors need it
choices.why: Replies are established, not new.

choices.text: A taken-over server calling out for instructions is stopped, and shows in the counters
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: It stops the DMZ from resolving names
choices.why: Unrelated.

prompt: How many rules on fw start with iifname "eth1", the DMZ?
hint: grep -c counted them.

prompt: app reached db on 5432 although no rule allows it. Why?
hint: Where do those packets travel?

choices.text: They are on one segment and never cross fw
choices.why: Right. The switch carries them.

choices.text: The baseline allows servers to talk among themselves
choices.why: No such rule; none could apply.

choices.text: db answers everybody on 5432
choices.why: From the internet it was blocked.

choices.text: established,related matched
choices.why: The packets never reached fw's rules.

prompt: Match each answer to machines on one segment reaching each other with where the course takes it.
hint: The table at the end of the section.

prompt: An office splits its LAN into three VLANs, and the core switch routes between them. What has the split achieved?
hint: Where is the traffic between VLANs filtered?

choices.text: Full segmentation, just as a firewall between them gives
choices.why: Nothing filters between them.

choices.text: Encryption of traffic between VLANs
choices.why: VLANs encrypt nothing.

choices.text: Little, unless routing between them crosses a firewall
choices.why: Right. A switch routing by itself undoes it.

choices.text: It stops broadcasts from crossing, which is the main risk
choices.why: Broadcasts are not the risk the lesson means.

prompt: The finance team asks for their reporting tool on the staff LAN to read the database on db, port 5432. Which change fits the matrix's discipline?
hint: One cell, as narrow as it can be.

choices.text: Allow the staff LAN to reach the servers segment
choices.why: That opens every server to every desk.

choices.text: Move db to the staff LAN
choices.why: The database would then share the least trusted zone.

choices.text: A rule from the reporting machine's address to db on 5432, with a comment naming the request
choices.why: Right. One cell, one source, one port.

choices.text: Turn off the policy drop during working hours
choices.why: Every empty cell would open.

prompt: Order the steps for changing the network's policy.
hint: Decide, write, prove.
items: change the cell in the zone matrix
write the rule with a comment naming the cell
probe the cell from the zone where it starts
trap: The matrix is the decision; the rule records it; only the probe shows what it does.

prompt: A new public service, a mail relay, has to be reachable from the internet. Where does it go?
hint: Reachable from the internet, a compromise costs little.

choices.text: On the servers segment, beside the database
choices.why: The internet would then reach the most trusted zone.

choices.text: In the DMZ
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: On the management segment
choices.why: The zone that administers everything is the last place for it.

choices.text: On the staff LAN, where the people who read mail are
choices.why: People's computers should not be reachable from outside.
